articles.title: Rise of AI Patents and their Corresponding Eligibility Rejections
articles.content:
美国专利商标局（USPTO）几年前开发了一个AI专利分类器，用于识别与人工智能相关的专利申请。我利用该分类器更新了至2026年的活动数据。结果发现，AI相关申请遭遇的101条款（专利适格性）拒绝比例明显高于非AI申请。例如，在2025年首次收到官方行动的申请中，包含AI的申请有42%被101条款拒绝，而非AI申请的拒绝率仅为6.9%。下图显示，两类申请在显而易见性（103条款）拒绝率方面几乎无差异，均保持在80%左右。

从图表可以看出，新冠疫情前的《专利适格性指南修订》将AI相关申请的101条款拒绝率减少了一半。然而，到2025年，这一减少效果几乎消失。相比之下，非AI申请的适格性拒绝率并未上升。根据现有数据，尚难判断这种变化是否与申请人提交内容的调整有关，还是美国专利商标局审查标准的变化。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

A few years ago the USPTO created an AI-patent classifier that identifies AI related patent applications.  I used that classifier to update activity through 2026. No surprise, AI application receive substantially more 101 eligibility rejections than their non-AI counterparts. An example - among applications whose first office action came in 2025, 42% of those containing AI have so far drawn a § 101 rejection, against 6.9% of those without.  The chart below shows no difference between the two categories for obviousness rejections, both of which hover close to 80%.

As you can see from the chart, the pre-COVID Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance cut the AI §101 rate about in half.  By 2025 that reduction has essentially disappeared. Whereas the eligibility rejection rate in non-AI applications  has not risen. From this data, I cannot tell the extent that the change is tied to changes by applicants in what is being filed or instead changes at the USPTO.

articles.title: SCOTUS: Patent Owner Joins the Section 314(d) Cert Queue
articles.content:
联邦快递向最高法院申请审查，以决定是否任何法院都能要求专利局遵守《美国专利法》第312(a)(2)条款，即要求IPR申请人披露"所有真实利益相关方"。在《联邦快递公司诉高通公司》（Federal Express Corp. v. Qualcomm Inc.，案号26-170）一案中，联邦快递请求审查联邦巡回法院的判决，该判决由休吉斯法官主笔，崔宁汉姆法官和斯塔克法官参与，案号为174 F.4th 910（2026年）。在本案中，专利审查委员会拒绝决定高通公司的IPR申请是否披露了所有真实利益相关方，然后仍然取消了相关专利权利要求。联邦巡回法院认为这种拒绝不可上诉，因为基于第312(a)(2)条款的挑战"归根结底是关于是否应该启动IPR程序的问题"。

专利局局长斯奎尔斯已经推翻了相关政策，但仍主张上诉法院无权审查。这是目前五起正在审理的关于第314(d)条款适用范围的申请之一，也是第一起由专利权人提出的。谷歌诉VirtaMove（案号25-1230）、英特尔诉斯奎尔斯（案号26-73）、特斯拉诉Granite Vehicle Ventures（案号26-136），以及尚未立案的Kahoot！案件，均由挑战者提出，指控专利局拒绝启动IPR程序。联邦快递则投诉相反的情况：专利局在未满足法定前提条件的情况下启动并审理了案件。今年早些时候，最高法院拒绝了杜比实验室许可公司诉统一专利公司（案号25-1011）案的证审请求，该案提出了相同的问题，涉及相同的行政实践。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

FedEx has asked the Supreme Court to decide whether any court can make the Patent Office follow 35 U.S.C. § 312(a)(2), the requirement that an IPR petitioner identify "all real parties in interest." The petition in Federal Express Corp. v. Qualcomm Inc., No. 26-170, seeks review of the Federal Circuit's precedential decision in Federal Express Corp. v. Qualcomm Inc., 174 F.4th 910 (Fed. Cir. 2026), where Judge Hughes wrote for a panel including Judges Cunningham and Stark. The Board in that case refused to decide whether Qualcomm's IPR petitions had named all real parties in interest, then went ahead and cancelled claims. The Federal Circuit held the refusal unreviewable because a challenge grounded in § 312(a)(2) "boils down to a challenge over whether there should have been institution at all."

Director Squires has reversed the underlying policy, but still argued that it was unreviewable on appeal.

This is the fifth petition now pending on the reach of § 314(d), and the first from the patent owner's side of the table. Google LLC v. VirtaMove, Corp., No. 25-1230, Intel Corp. v. Squires, No. 26-73, Tesla, Inc. v. Granite Vehicle Ventures LLC, No. 26-136, and the still-undocketed Kahoot! petition all come from challengers complaining that the Office will not institute. See Dennis Crouch, Four Petitions, One Question: Tesla Joins the Supreme Court's IPR Reviewability Docket, Patently-O (July 30, 2026). FedEx complains about the opposite: the Office instituted and adjudicated without satisfying a statutory precondition. Earlier this summer the Court denied certiorari in Dolby Laboratories Licensing Corp. v. Unified Patents, LLC, No. 25-1011, which raised the same question about the same agency practice.
